podcast.body: Featured on the 1970 album of the same name, this song clearly displays Tony Iomi's tri tone, played with a trill and distortion. Iomi's inspiration for this sound came from Gustav Holst's "Mars, the Bringer of War," which he adapted by slowing it down and adding distortion, marking it as a pivotal moment for the birth of heavy metal. "And you can clearly hear Iomi's tri tone played with a little bit of a trill. For some, this is the birth of heavy metal."

podcast.body: The band, originally named Earth, changed its name after Ozzy Osbourne penned the lyrics for this song. The lyrics feature dark, ominous imagery, including a "figure in black," "big black shape with eyes of fire," and escalating flames, culminating in "Oh no, no, please God help me." Despite the chilling content, Ozzy Osbourne stated in 1978 that the band was not satanic and merely aimed to "create a brand to sell the band." "The band that at one time was called Earth, that changed its name to black Sabbath after Ozzy Osborne wrote the lyrics to the song, black Sabbath."
